newsitem.title: THAILAND: Finance One downplays insider trade probe.
newsitem.headline: Finance One downplays insider trade probe.

text.p: The president of Thailand's top finance company, Finance One, on Friday downplayed news that the nation's securities watchdog was probing his firm's executives for possible insider trading.
"What I had sold is considered minimal compared to the total amount of shares I have," Pin Chakkaphak told reporters after signing a merger pact between Finance One and Thai Danu Bank Plc.
The Securities and Exchange Commission said on Friday it was investigating transactions involving Finance One officials to see if they had violated insider trading regulations.
Prasarn Trairatvorakul, the SEC deputy secretary general, said the firm's executives had sold a substantial amount of the company's shares since last year.
Prasarn said the SEC was obliged to carry out the investigation because these transactions happened before Finance One revealed its plans to merge with Thai Danu.
The two institutions announced the merger on March 3.
SEC sources said Pin along with his family members and other executives, sold millions of shares between the second half of last year and early 1997.
